_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ems__Bug 6b4d2533 — SUBJECT: packages/core/src/utilities/yamlScalar.ts. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout. Guards enumerated from `git diff -U0` of the fix (integration-test-revert-verify §A8): the new rule in needsYamlQuoting, its range gate, the number-only filter (Date and boolean excluded), the 1.2-core agreement exclusion and the defensive catch. The harness also runs the existing yamlScalar / MetadataHelpers / FrontmatterService quoting suites, and `red_re` catches EVERY axis name (`[A-Z]\d+[a-z]?`), not only Y — so an existing axis a mutant reddens is listed in `expect` with its reason (review of PR #4590, MEDIUM-2: with a Y-only `red_re` those extra axes were invisible).

M1_rule_removed._note: The fix itself: without the rule the writer returns to the pre-fix shape and `18:00` is written bare (Y1, Y3, Y4 — the reported defect) along with `+.5` (Y2). R19 reds too: its rewritten control line expects `10:30` quoted on an untyped property — the same rule, pinned in the req 21ceea14 suite (measured, §A44).

M2_range_gate_dropped._note: Without the gate a DECLARED range stops deciding the typing: `1:30.5` under xsd:decimal and `18:00` under xsd:integer get quoted, overriding ticket 2227d660 (Y7, Y8). R22 reds too: it pins declared numeric ranges in the 8185c9dd suite (measured, §A44).

M3_date_admitted.to: if (typeof v === "string" || v === null || v === undefined) return false;
M3_date_admitted._note: Admits a Date (and a boolean) as a disagreement: a bare datetime is quoted and timestamp properties would stop being xsd:dateTime (Y6; R18a/R18b pin the same datetime bound in the 8185c9dd suite). ⛔ Y9 (1.1 booleans stay bare) does NOT redden: the pre-filter `MAYBE_YAML11_ONLY_NUMBER` already rejects `yes` / `no` before the load, so Y9 is held by TWO guards and no single mutant can redden it — stated, not hidden (§A33); M7 (pre-filter removed) is the other half and is zero for the same reason.

M4_agreement_exclusion_dropped._note: Drops the 'both readers agree' exclusion: a bare `3` or `1.5` would be quoted and untyped numbers would turn into strings (Y5). R5/R10/R11/G2 pin bare numbers on non-string properties in the existing suites (measured, §A44).

M5_catch_returns_true.from:
// a value the reader rejects, written bare, breaks the whole frontmatter.
    return true;
M5_catch_returns_true.to:

M5_catch_returns_true._note: ⛔ Defensive branch, no distinguishing input (integration-test-revert-verify §A35): every value the reader rejects in `v: <value>` position is quoted by the guards needsYamlQuoting runs before the rule, so the catch is unreachable from the writer (fuzz of 1 170 675 forms in review of PR #4590: 0 reach it). The branch now fails towards quoting (LOW-3); this mutant flips it back to bare. Stated, not hidden; M1 is the canary that the delivery works.

M6_prefilter_drops_plus._note: The pre-filter must admit a leading `+`: `+.5` is a YAML 1.1-only number. Without `+` it slips past the rule and is written bare (Y2; Y3/Y4 carry `+.5` in their list).

M7_prefilter_removed._note: ⛔ Pure optimisation, no distinguishing input (§A35): the pre-filter only rejects values the number check rejects anyway — corpus of 160 436 values × 20 (qa, range) pairs, v1 (no pre-filter) vs v2: 0 differing (review of PR #4590 corpus, re-run 2026-11-02). It also holds Y9 together with the number check (see M3). Canary M1.

M8_string_semantics_skip_removed._note: ⛔ Pure optimisation, no distinguishing input (§A35): under string semantics the oracle `looksLikeNonStringScalar` below already quotes every YAML 1.1-only number, so skipping the rule there only saves the second `yaml.load` (LOW-4). Same corpus: 0 differing. Canary M1.
